Vivek / Lauren — draft below for the checklist. I kept it concise for procurement. Feel free to edit.

1) Sampling policy (hosted vs dedicated)
- Hosted API: default adaptive sampling — base 1% random sample of outputs; automatic up-sampling on policy signals (keywords, high-confidence classifiers) to up to 10% for 24h windows. Customers can configure sampling by route/model via Console.
- Dedicated: sampling is configurable by tenant; default is 0.5% to minimise telemetry egress. We recommend 1% for high-risk workloads; automatic up-sampling available if customer enables telemetry routing to Redwood's telemetry plane.

2) Triggered sampling (both modes)
- Triggers: classifier score threshold, user abuse reports, anomalous request patterns (burst >3x baseline), manual sampling requests from customer security.
- On trigger: immediate full-request capture for the affected session + 72h increased sample rate.

3) Notification cadence & channels
- Critical incidents (active exploitation or PII leakage): immediate page to configured security contacts + email summary within 1 hour.
- High-priority suspicious trends: daily digest during triage window (24h) + weekly executive summary.
- Low-priority noise: queued for weekly review; customers can opt-in to real-time streams.

4) Evidence preservation & TTLs
- Live KV + streaming logs retained for 72h by default (hosted). Archived artifacts (de-identified request/response bundles + metadata) retained for 365 days by default in object storage; retention configurable.
- Dedicated deployments: between customer-controlled retention and Redwood-managed retention depending on network model; retention and egress costs documented in Console.

5) Access & audit
- Role-based access for retrieval; all evidence retrieval requests logged. Support for signed audit exports (CSV) and SOC2-ready audit trails.

6) Privacy controls
- Automatic PII scrubbing by default for hosted when customers opt-in; dedicated customers can bring their own scrubbing policies.

Notes: I'll attach a sampling matrix CSV and our redact/PII checklist.

Adding deployment/ops bullets and small edits to wording for procurement:

- Hosted defaults are configurable per-account via Console; retention toggles and sampling overrides are exposed in the "Telemetry" page. We document token-level redaction and costs associated with long-term archiving in the pricing appendix.
- Dedicated: for VPC/private deployments we provide an agent that streams telemetry to customer-managed storage (S3/GCS) and an option to mirror only metadata to Redwood's control plane for alerting.
- Key management: hosted uses Redwood KMS (customer-managed keys supported); Dedicated supports BYOK via Cloud HSM or local KMS gateway.
- Evidence export: standard export formats (JSONL, CSV) plus a forensics bundle (tar.gz) that includes timestamps, model/version, tokenizer state, and classifier scores.

Marissa attached a ready-to-share evidence bundle and a short cover letter for FalconPay procurement.

-LB
